blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Pretrained video diffusion models (VDMs) offer a powerful foundation for World Action Models (WAMs), which jointly predict robot actions and future observations. Building such models requires injecting low-dimensional robot signals (e.g. proprioception, actions, and values) into a latent space shaped by natural videos, and a key design choice is the interface through which these signals enter: existing schemes treat it as a formatting detail, spending a separate latent frame on each signal or bolting on dedicated encoders and decoders. We argue that signal injection is instead a distribution-alignment problem: how well a representation matches the prior of the pretrained VDMs during denoising. Using the relative reconstruction error of a frozen VDM denoiser as a probe, we find that conventional spatial encodings sit far off this prior, whereas frequency-domain packing yields latents that the denoiser corrects far less. Motivated by this diagnostic result, we propose MetaWAM, which folds all robot signals into a single unified meta-frame: each signal is assigned to a disjoint frequency-domain channel band and lifted to the spatial latent by an inverse DCT, yielding a decodable interface aligned with the pretrained VDM prior without any added module or architectural change. A fixed band layout together with slot-aware routing lets the same meta-frame support policy, world-model, and value prediction over a shared set of robot variables. On RoboCasa, MetaWAM reaches 68.9% success while collapsing the per-signal frames into one and cutting inference latency by 39%, and attains 85.0% success on three real-world Franka tasks. Code and models are available at https://github.com/showlab/MetaWAM
blocks.zh: 预先训练的视频传播模型(VDMs)为"世界行动模型"(WAMS)提供了强大的基础,后者共同预测了机器人行动和未来观测. 构建这样的模型需要将低维机器人信号(如自发,动作和值等)注入由自然视频所塑造的潜在空间,关键的设计选择是这些信号进入的界面:现有方案将它视为格式化的细节,在每个信号上单独花出一个潜在框架,或者在专用编码器和解码器上螺栓. 我们主张,信号注射是一个分布-对接问题:在解密时,一种表示方式如何与预先训练的VDM之前匹配。 利用被冻结的 VDM denoiser 作为探测器的相对重建错误, 我们发现常规的空间编码 远比这早, 而频率域的包装 产生潜伏, enoiser 纠正的要少得多。 基于这个诊断结果,我们提出MetaWAM,它将所有机器人信号折叠成一个单一的统一元帧:每个信号被分配到一个断接频域通道波段并被反向的DCT提升到空间潜伏,产生一个与预先训练的VDM一致的可解码界面,之前没有添加任何模块或建筑变化. 固定的波段布局加上有槽意识的路由,让相同的元帧支持政策,世界模型,以及价值预测对一组共享的机器人变量进行. 在RoboCasa上,MetaWAM取得了68.9%的成功率,同时将每个信号框拆为一并切入推论延迟了39%,并在三个现实世界的Franka任务上取得了85.0%的成功. 守则和模型见https://github.com/showlab/MetaWAM。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Vision-Language-Action models have become a powerful paradigm for generalist robot
control, yet they learn reactive observation-to-action mappings without modeling how the world
evolves under their actions [ 1 ] . World Action Models (WAMs) close this gap by adapting pretrained video diffusion models
(VDMs), which carry strong spatiotemporal priors over scene dynamics, to predict actions and
future observations jointly.
Existing WAMs differ mainly in how they couple world prediction and control. Cascaded WAMs use the video model as a learned simulator and recover actions through a separate
inverse-dynamics model or policy [ 2 , 3 , 4 ] , while Joint WAMs let one
generative backbone emit actions, future observations, and values within a single denoising
process [ 5 , 6 ] . Across these designs, a key interface is often
treated as a formatting detail: how low-dimensional robot variables, such as proprioception,
actions, task type, and values, should enter a latent space shaped by natural-video statistics.
This raises the question: how should structured robot signals be represented so that a
pretrained VDM treats them as in-distribution during denoising?

blocks.en:
A straightforward solution injects each robot signal as its own video-like latent frame,
either by spatially tiling the raw signal across the frame [ 5 ] or by
rendering it into an image and re-encoding it through the pretrained VAE [ 7 ] ;
both preserve backbone compatibility but inflate the sequence length and the quadratic attention
cost it incurs. Other designs attach dedicated action encoders or decoders [ 6 ] ,
improving action modeling at the cost of modifying the pretrained backbone. We view signal
injection as a distribution-alignment problem: a useful representation must remain
compatible with the VDM prior seen by the pretrained denoiser. As previewed in
Fig. 1 (b), frequency-domain encoding produces latents that the frozen denoiser
corrects far less than spatial encodings.

blocks.en:
To examine this design space, we run diagnostic experiments that trace candidate injections through
VDM denoising, covering both single-signal injection and multi-signal packing, and measure how
strongly a frozen denoiser corrects the injected latent across noise levels. These experiments show
that the arrangement of robot signals in latent space measurably affects the denoiser:
frequency-domain packing yields latents it corrects far less than spatial tiling or discontinuous
canvas layouts. Compactness alone is therefore insufficient; an effective interface must be distribution-aware .

blocks.en:
Motivated by these findings, we propose MetaWAM, which folds all heterogeneous robot signals into
a single unified meta-frame (Fig. 1 (a)). Rather than allocating a latent frame
to each signal, MetaWAM assigns every signal, including current and future proprioception, action
chunks, task type, and value, to a disjoint frequency-domain channel band within one frame, and
lifts the packed coefficients to the spatial latent via an analytical inverse DCT. This produces
smooth latent patterns well aligned with the pretrained denoiser, while a single meta-frame becomes
a multiplexed carrier for many low-dimensional signals. The design requires no additional action
encoder, learned decoder, or modification to the denoising architecture, and recovers each signal
analytically at readout.

blocks.en:
We instantiate MetaWAM on a Cosmos-Predict2 backbone and evaluate it on RoboCasa, LIBERO,
LIBERO-Plus, and three real-world Franka tabletop tasks. MetaWAM exceeds the RoboCasa frame-injection baseline while collapsing
multiple robot-signal frames into one. Our contributions are:
(1) we recast robot-signal injection as a distribution-aware latent-interface problem for Joint WAMs;
(2) we provide diagnostic evidence that frequency-domain packing aligns better with a pretrained
VDM prior than spatial signal encodings; and
(3) we introduce a unified frequency-domain meta-frame that carries all robot signals in a single
decoder-free latent frame without architectural changes.

2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
World Action Models. World Action Models (WAMs) recast robot control as generative modeling over future states and
actions [ 1 ] . Cascaded WAMs generate or represent future observations first and
then recover actions through a separate policy or inverse-dynamics model [ 2 , 3 , 8 ] . Joint WAMs instead couple action and future-state prediction inside
one backbone. Cosmos Policy [ 5 ] injects actions, proprioception, future
states, and values as additional latent frames, preserving the pretrained video architecture;
DreamZero [ 6 ] uses dedicated action encoders and decoders around a video
backbone; and UWM/UVA [ 9 , 10 ] decouple video and action diffusion schedules to
enable mixed robot and video training. Recent efficiency-oriented WAMs reduce inference cost by
changing what is denoised or attended to, such as removing future-frame generation at test
time [ 11 ] or emphasizing action-centered decoding [ 12 ] .
MetaWAM is orthogonal to these directions: it keeps the pretrained denoising architecture intact
but changes how robot signals are represented inside the latent sequence. Rather than treating
signal injection as a formatting choice, we study its compatibility with the pretrained VDM prior
and introduce a distribution-aware interface.

blocks.en:
Latent signal representations. A broad line of work studies how robot or agent signals should be encoded into compact latent
forms. Learned schemes include VQ-VAE latent action codes derived from visual
dynamics [ 13 , 14 ] , world-model-grounded latent actions [ 15 ] , highly
compressed discrete action chunks [ 16 ] , and modality-specific latent positions for
proprioception, actions, and future tokens [ 17 ] . Transform-based schemes exploit
frequency structure: FAST [ 18 ] applies 1D DCT to robot action sequences, while
wavelet tokenizers [ 19 ] , FA-VAE [ 20 ] , and
DocPedia [ 21 ] use frequency-domain representations for visual or document
modeling. MetaWAM differs in target and mechanism: it uses channel-wise 2D DCT bands to pack
heterogeneous robot signals directly into the latent space of a pretrained VDM, lifts them back to
the spatial domain by analytical iDCT, and recovers them without a learned decoder.

drawn from real RoboCasa observations, and we evaluate this error across noise levels σ \sigma .

off-prior. Fig. 2 and Tab. 1 summarize the
schemes and results.

blocks.en:
Multi-signal packing. We use the corresponding action chunks, proprioceptive states, and value labels from the
same RoboCasa samples to compare four layouts (Fig. 2 (d–g)). Separate Spatial Duplication spatially duplicates each signal into its own latent
frame, using three frames in total; its reported error is averaged over these frames. Meta-Quadrants puts all three signals into one frame, assigning each an equally sized
spatial region and replicating its values along the channel dimension within that region. Meta-Compact also uses one frame and channel-wise replication, but allocates spatial
regions according to signal dimensionality: action chunks occupy a larger region, while
proprioception and value occupy smaller ones. These two layouts therefore test whether
spatial consolidation alone, with either equal or dimension-dependent allocation, is sufficient.
Our Unified Meta-Frame instead assigns signals to disjoint channel bands, writes their
values into fixed DCT coefficient slots, and applies a per-channel 2D inverse DCT to form
one spatial latent. Signals are separated by channel allocation rather than spatial boundaries.

blocks.en:
Takeaway. Two principles follow. First, injection must be distribution-aware , since compactness alone
does not guarantee compatibility with the VDM’s natural-video prior. Second, multi-signal WAMs
should not spend a full latent frame per low-dimensional signal.
MetaWAM further adopts a decoder-free design, recovering signals analytically so that the savings from fewer
frames are not offset by added modules. The method below realizes these choices as a unified
frequency-domain meta-frame with slot-aware task routing. Further analysis on the
Wan-based [ 23 ] backbone is provided in the supplementary material.

blocks.en: 4 Method
blocks.zh: 4 方法

blocks.en:
We introduce MetaWAM, a World Action Model built around a unified robot-signal latent
interface (Fig. 3 ).
Rather than design a new backbone, we rethink how
structured robot variables enter an existing pretrained VDM, replacing frame-wise injection with
a pair of compact meta-frames : an input meta-frame for robot-state conditioning and an
output meta-frame for action, future-state, and value prediction. Each meta-frame exposes its
variables not as raw spatial patterns but through structured frequency bands, turning one frame
into a multiplexed carrier for many low-dimensional signals while preserving the denoising architecture and removing redundant latent frames.

blocks.en:

from the current state; the world model predicts the future state from state and action; value
estimation predicts the return from the full transition. The variables never move between
frames; they always occupy the same channel bands of the output meta-frame, and only their role changes per task.

blocks.en: A.1 Experiment Details
blocks.zh: A.1 实验细节

blocks.en:
All motivating-analysis experiments are conducted using samples from the RoboCasa dataset [ 24 ] released with Cosmos Policy [ 5 ] .
For the single-signal analysis, we randomly select 30 action chunks from distinct episodes and compare different ways of injecting this low-dimensional signal into the latent space.
For the multi-signal packing analysis, we use the corresponding action chunks, proprioceptive states, and value labels to construct packed meta-frame variants, allowing us to evaluate the distributional compatibility of different multi-signal encoding schemes under the same pretrained video diffusion model.
blocks.zh:
所有动力分析实验都是利用用宇宙政策释放的RoboCasa数据集样本进行的。
对于单信号分析,我们随机从不同的片段中选择30个动作块,并比较将这种低维信号注入潜在空间的不同方式.
对于多信号包装分析,我们使用相应的动作块,自控状态,以及价值标签来构建装填的元帧变体,使我们能够评价不同多信号编码方案的分布兼容性,使用同一预先训练的视频传播模型.

blocks.en:
We compare three spatial packing baselines against our frequency-domain meta-frame. Sep. Spatial Dup. follows the Cosmos Policy implementation, where different robot-related signals are injected into separate latent frames by spatially duplicating each signal across the latent grid. Meta-Quadrants packs multiple signals into a single latent frame by assigning each signal to an equally sized spatial region, and then replicating the signal values along the channel dimension within its assigned region. Meta-Compact also uses a single latent frame but allocates spatial regions according to signal dimensionality: longer signals, such as action chunks, occupy larger regions, while shorter signals, such as proprioception and value, use smaller regions.
As in Meta-Quadrants, the assigned signal values are replicated along the channel dimension within each spatial region.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了三个空间包装基线 与我们的频率域元框架。 Sep. Space Dup. 遵循宇宙政策的实施,通过在空间上重复跨越潜在网格的每个信号,将不同的机器人相关信号注入单独的潜伏框架。 Meta-Quadrants将多个信号打包成一个单一的潜在框架,将每个信号分配给一个大小相同的空间区域,然后在指定区域内沿信道维度复制信号值. Meta-Compact还使用一个单一的潜伏框架,但根据信号维度来分配空间区域:较长的信号,如动作块,占据更大的区域,而较短的信号,如自主和值,则使用较小的区域.

blocks.en: A.2 Cross-Backbone Analysis on Wan2.1 and Wan2.2
blocks.zh: A.2 关于Wan2.1和Wan2.2的交叉包骨分析

blocks.en:
To further examine whether the observed advantage of frequency-domain encoding is specific to Cosmos-Predict2 [ 22 ] , we conduct the same motivating analysis on two additional video diffusion backbones from the Wan series [ 23 ] : Wan2.1-I2V-14B and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B.
As shown in Tab. 6 and Tab. 7 , DCT Encoding consistently achieves lower denoiser reconstruction error than spatial duplication and VAE-based encoding in the single-signal injection setting, while our Unified Meta-Frame outperforms all spatial packing baselines in the multi-signal packing setting.
These results demonstrate that the benefit of frequency-domain signal injection is not tied to a particular model size, video-diffusion backbone, or training objective.
Specifically, the same trend holds across Wan2.1-I2V-14B and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B, which are trained with flow matching, as well as Cosmos-Predict2, which follows an EDM-style residual denoising formulation.
This cross-backbone consistency further supports our claim that DCT-based meta-frames provide a more VDM-compatible interface for injecting low-dimensional robot signals into pretrained video diffusion models.

blocks.en: The LIBERO benchmark [ 25 ] includes four primary task suites: LIBERO-Spatial, LIBERO-Object, LIBERO-Goal, and LIBERO-Long. Each task suite provides a training dataset of 500 demonstrations in total, covering 10 tasks with 50 demonstrations per task. We follow the standard evaluation protocol used by prior works [ 5 , 45 ] . For each suite, success rates are averaged over 500 evaluation trials, corresponding to 10 tasks with 50 episodes per task. We evaluate each method with three random seeds, resulting in 6000 evaluation trials in total across the four LIBERO suites. We train MetaWAM on LIBERO for 12K optimization steps using 4 NVIDIA H200 GPUs with a global batch size of 1200, requiring 56 hours of wall-clock training time. The policy predicts an action chunk of 16 timesteps, and we execute all steps before re-querying the policy, following the setting of Cosmos Policy [ 5 ] .

blocks.en:
In the unified policy, world-model, and value setting, a robot signal can serve as a clean
condition or a prediction target depending on the task. A learned interface therefore needs
per-signal encoding and decoding together with mask-aware routing; updating its encoders
also changes the latent targets presented to the denoiser. A zero-initialized projection
initially conveys no signal. Fixed packing and DCT/iDCT instead provide a static analytical
mapping and readout from the start of training. The observed optimization behavior supports
this design for the tested setup, without implying that learned interfaces cannot work with
other architectures or training procedures.
